entries.title: Invention and Prototype Crafting System
entries.summary: A converted Hypertext d20 downtime system for researching, financing, building, testing, repairing, and improving inventions.
body: Kaysender inventions include mechanical devices, arcane apparatus, ship systems, weapons, armor modifications, navigation instruments, alchemical tools, constructed defenses, new spells, and enchanted components. The procedure is designed for projects whose design and testing matter enough to become part of play.

Every project begins with a written design brief: the intended function, target user or vessel, operating conditions, complexity, materials, facility, primary construction skill, and any magical requirements. The GM should approve the result before costs are paid.

A project advances through research, procurement, construction, testing, and optional improvement. Checks create consequences rather than repeatedly asking whether the character is allowed to try. A failed roll can consume time, introduce a flaw, damage materials, or reveal that a new approach is required.

sections.heading: Project complexity and work units
body: Routine project — DC 10, 1 work unit: a known design, common repair, basic trap, ordinary tool, or simple modification.
Standard project — DC 15, 3 work units: a dependable field device, improved tool, minor vehicle component, alchemical apparatus, or modest permanent item.
Complex project — DC 20, 6 work units: a specialized gadget, advanced ship component, unusual permanent item, or device combining several systems.
Advanced project — DC 25, 12 work units: a powerful prototype, major vessel installation, autonomous apparatus, or item with several significant functions.
Revolutionary project — DC 30, 24 work units: a unique breakthrough, new engine principle, major magical invention, or campaign-defining technology.

One work unit equals eight hours of productive labor by one qualified primary crafter in a suitable facility. Each successful construction check completes 1 work unit, plus 1 additional work unit for every 5 points by which the result exceeds the project DC.

sections.heading: Skills, assistance, and facilities
body: Choose one primary skill appropriate to the design: Craft (mechanical), Craft (weaponsmithing), Craft (armorsmithing), Craft (trapmaking), Craft (alchemy), Craft (shipwright), Knowledge (arcana), Spellcraft, or another specific Craft approved by the GM.
A second relevant skill may support research or testing but cannot replace the primary construction skill without redesigning the project.
Up to three qualified assistants may use aid another. An assistant must have at least 1 rank in a relevant skill and must contribute for the same work period.

An improvised workspace imposes a -2 circumstance penalty. A proper workshop provides no modifier. A specialized laboratory, shipyard bay, enchanting circle, or master workshop provides a +2 circumstance bonus when genuinely suited to the project.
Crafting aboard a moving or damaged vessel may impose penalties for turbulence, interruption, inadequate power, or unsafe access.

sections.heading: Cost, materials, and financing
body: The expected market price is set by comparison with existing equipment and the project’s campaign impact. Raw materials normally cost one-third of that market price.

Improvised or reclaimed materials cost about 75 percent of the normal raw-material budget and impose a -2 circumstance penalty on construction and testing. Fine materials cost 150 percent and grant +2. Exceptional or purpose-built materials cost 300 percent and grant +4.
Rare components, legal permits, proprietary plans, magical services, and dangerous fuel are separate requirements rather than abstract additions to the material cost.
A patron may finance a project, but ownership, delivery rights, reporting obligations, secrecy, and liability should be established before construction begins.

sections.heading: Research, construction, and testing procedure
body: Research: Spend at least one day and attempt a relevant Knowledge, Spellcraft, Profession, or Craft check against the project DC. Success grants +2 on the first construction check; exceeding the DC by 5 grants +4 instead. Failure by 4 or less provides no modifier. Failure by 5 or more imposes -2 until the design is revised through another day of research.

Procurement: Acquire the listed materials and facility. A Survival, Appraise, Gather Information, Knowledge, or Profession check may locate rare components, but acquiring them can still require payment, travel, negotiation, or an adventure.

Construction: At the end of each work unit, attempt the primary construction check. Success completes progress. Failure by 1–4 completes no progress and wastes materials equal to 10 percent of the remaining raw-material budget. Failure by 5–9 also creates a minor flaw. Failure by 10 or more causes a major accident, destroys at least 25 percent of remaining materials, and requires repair or redesign before work continues.

Testing: When all work units are complete, spend at least one hour operating the item under realistic conditions and attempt the primary skill or a designated testing skill against the project DC. Success validates the invention. Exceeding the DC by 5 identifies a minor optimization that can be applied without additional cost. Failure reveals a flaw; failure by 5 or more triggers the flaw during testing and may damage the invention or operator.
Certification: Guilds, governments, ship owners, insurers, or military commands may require a separate inspection before an invention can be legally installed, sold, or operated.

sections.heading: Flaws and accidents
body: Minor flaw examples: unreliable activation, +25 percent maintenance cost, -2 on one narrow use, reduced range, loud operation, visible smoke, awkward weight, one fewer daily use, or mandatory recalibration after strenuous use.

Major flaw examples: dangerous feedback, doubled fuel consumption, random shutdown, damage to the operator on a failed check, interference with adjacent systems, structural weakness, or inability to function in one common environment.

A catastrophic accident may cause an explosion, fire, toxic release, uncontrolled magical effect, hull breach, destroyed workshop, injured assistants, legal investigation, or faction interest. The consequence should match the project's scale and materials.
A known flaw can be repaired as an improvement project. Concealing a flaw from a buyer, captain, guild, or regulator creates an independent legal and reputational risk.

sections.heading: Improvement and reverse engineering
body: Improving a working invention is a new project at the original complexity DC +5. It normally costs 25 percent of the item’s market price and requires work units equal to one-quarter of the original project, rounded up.

A successful improvement should add one bounded benefit: +1 on a narrow check, 25 percent greater range or capacity, 25 percent lower fuel or maintenance cost, removal of one flaw, one additional daily use, reduced setup time, or a similarly limited function.

Reverse engineering requires access to a functioning example for at least one day and a research check at DC 5 higher than the original project. Success produces a usable design brief; it does not supply rare materials, legal rights, magical prerequisites, or proprietary workshop techniques.
No item can receive more than three improvements without being rebuilt as a project of the next higher complexity.

sections.heading: Interaction with class abilities
body: Airship Engineer class gadgets are temporary field devices created through class resources and do not require this full downtime procedure. Permanently reproducing a gadget uses this system.
Ship Engineer and Shipwright Captain features can provide repair, inspection, and workshop advantages but do not erase material costs or certification requirements.
Tinker Engineer trap and gadget features represent prepared adventuring resources. Permanent traps, commercial production, and large installations use normal project complexity.
Spells and magic items require the appropriate caster level, item-creation feat, spell access, or equivalent setting prerequisite in addition to invention checks.
